endorsements.quote: To avoid unexpected biases and obsolescence, we must continuously benchmark AI performance on target populations and enable automated or semiautomated self-adaptation mechanisms to these changes.

Besides benchmarking model performance in clinical indicators—for example, number of hospital readmissions in readmission prediction—or confusion matrix-derived metrics—for example, sensitivity and specificity—an RAI in production should monitor dataset shifts, user-defined DQ rules, user requirements—for example, deprecated or new International Classificafion of Diseases codes—and continuously benchmarking FRA.

unlisted_practices: Health AI should be designed to be resilient to real-world data quality issues, variability, uncertainty, and bias throughout training, prediction, and production.
AI outputs should include quantified uncertainty such as confidence intervals or levels, and warn users of high-uncertainty cases.
Any fully automated modification of missing, implausible, or outlying inputs should be notified to users and its effect on output quantified through sensitivity analysis.
AI predictions should be explainable and interpretable to support user adherence.
Developers should apply pretraining, in-training, and posttraining algorithmic bias mitigation methods for fundamental-rights-sensitive subpopulations.
Developers should tag data quality issues in training data and allow models to discard, fix, or learn from them.
Developers should validate the use of foundation models in clinical decision support and thoroughly quantify their risks and uncertainty.
Regulators should include specific resilience and self-adaptiveness provisions for self-adaptive health AI in regulations.
Developers should standardize documentation and record-keeping of rules that trigger AI self-adaptation and justify automated data curation.
Developers should compare current cases with similar past cases with validated outcomes and warn about potential fundamental rights violations.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint / framework article outlining challenges, requirements, methods, and a research agenda for trustworthy and resilient AI clinical decision support systems.
